subject: Elevated latency on streaming/chat endpoints — mitigation plan and follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Derek Howell <derek@amplify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Incident: Elevated latency on streaming/chat endpoints — immediate mitigations

Hi Derek —

We observed elevated end-to-end latency for streaming chat replies affecting requests to the us-west-2 cluster starting ~08:40 PDT. You may have seen incomplete streaming chunks and delayed first-token delivery for a subset of sessions.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (so you have context):
- Enabled circuit-breaker routing for Amplify.ai traffic to reduce in-flight concurrency on the affected shards.
- Temporarily routed new streaming sessions to a non-streaming fallback (short poll / chunked polling) while we stabilize streaming chunk delivery.
- Reduced default max_tokens for streaming paths from 1024 -> 512 to reduce token emission pressure for the next 60 minutes.
- Deployed a targeted runtime patch that forces KV-cache rehydration rather than on-the-fly merges which was blocking event loop under certain shard-rebalance conditions.

Technical summary (high level):
We are tracing this to a correlated sequence of shard rebalances in the us-west-2 inference pool that caused KV-cache contention in some runtime processes. That contention increased per-request tail-latency for streaming paths where the runtime attempted synchronous KV operations during first-token emission.

What we need from you now:
1) Can you confirm whether toggling to a non-streaming fallback for a short window is acceptable? That will preserve correctness while we complete the runtime fix.
2) If you prefer we can instead limit concurrency per API key — tell us desired QPS cap and we’ll apply it.

We know this is customer-impacting and are prioritizing. I will send a follow-up with a timeline and postmortem once the root cause is confirmed.

Attachments: latency-snapshot-0930.png (PNG), kv-cache-dump-05-30.txt (log excerpt)

Thanks —
Marcus Lin

Folks — quick internal note to capture actions and owners. I will publish a customer-facing postmortem after the incident but logging here for the team:

- 08:40:10 PDT: multiple shard rebalances detected (autoscaler activity + host drain).
- 08:40:55 PDT: runtime KV-cache contention increased; first-token emission latency spikes recorded.
- 08:42:00 PDT: routing rules adjusted; affected keys routed to fallback; mitigation applied.

Immediate owners / actions: 
- Marissa: confirm if customer credit is required and coordinate with CSM (target: 05/31 EOD).
- Hannah: work with runtime team to finalize the KV-cache rehydration patch going into canary (target: 09:00 PDT).
- Connor: apply temporary per-key concurrency cap if Derek requests it.
- Marcus (me): notify Amplify about fallback plan and track until streaming restored.

Customer-facing messaging: short, practical, and include precise next steps. Derek has okayed fallback. Our current ask is to provide an ETA for restoration and a summary postmortem within 24 hours.

- Marcus

Subject: Post-incident summary: streaming latency (Amplify.ai) — root cause & next steps

Hi Derek —

Thanks again for the fast coordination during yesterday's elevated latency event. Below is a short post-incident summary and concrete next steps.

What happened (short):
- Between ~08:39–08:42 PDT on 2028-05-30, concurrent shard rebalances in the us-west-2 inference pool caused synchronous KV-cache operations in a subset of runtime processes. Those synchronous operations increased tail latency for streaming paths (first-token and chunk handoff).

Impact:
- Approximately 1.7% of streaming sessions for Amplify.ai experienced delayed first-token emission and intermittent truncated chunks during the 3–4 minute window. No data loss; events were preserved server-side.

Root cause:
- Autoscaler-triggered host drains caused overlapping rehydration logic to run synchronously in live runtime threads. The rehydration path was not resilient to concurrent merges which resulted in intermediate blocking on the event loop.

Actions completed:
- Deployed a targeted runtime patch (fix/runtime/kv-rehydrate-2028-05-30) that forces asynchronous rehydration and backpressure-aware batching.
- Adjusted routing policy to avoid scheduling critical sessions onto draining hosts during autoscaler events.
- Temporarily offered non-streaming fallback for affected sessions; we reverted to normal streaming at 10:12 PDT after canary validation.

Planned longer-term fixes (ETA):
- Q3 2028: Rewrite of the KV rehydration module to eliminate synchronous merges and add per-shard background reconciliation (owner: runtime infra).
- Q3 2028: Improved autoscaler stutter detection to avoid overlapping drains (owner: infra autoscaler team).

Compensation:
- Marissa will follow up regarding a one-time usage credit for the impacted window (we aim to propose this by 2028-05-31 EOD).

Attachments: incident timeline, KV cache diagnostics excerpt, link to patch and rollback notes.

If you'd like, we can set up a 30-minute bridge to walk through the technical details with your engineers. Would Monday morning (PDT) work?

Best —
